# Get-ZbxAuditLog

## SYNOPSIS

Gets the audit log records that say who changed what.

## SYNTAX

### All (Default)

```
Get-ZbxAuditLog [-Limit <int>] [-SortField <string[]>] [-User <ZabbixReference<ZabbixUser>[]>] [-From <DateTimeOffset>] [-Till <DateTimeOffset>] [-InputObject <PSObject>] [-SortOrder <ZabbixSortOrder[]>] [-Search <Hashtable>] [-SearchByAny] [-StartSearch] [-ExcludeSearch] [-SearchWildcardsEnabled] [-CountOutput] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-First <UInt64>] [-Skip <UInt64>] [-IncludeTotalCount] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### ByFilter

```
Get-ZbxAuditLog [-SortField <string[]>] -Filter <ZabbixAuditLogGetParameters> [-User <ZabbixReference<ZabbixUser>[]>] [-From <DateTimeOffset>] [-Till <DateTimeOffset>] [-InputObject <PSObject>] [-SortOrder <ZabbixSortOrder[]>] [-Search <Hashtable>] [-SearchByAny] [-StartSearch] [-ExcludeSearch] [-SearchWildcardsEnabled] [-CountOutput] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-First <UInt64>] [-Skip <UInt64>] [-IncludeTotalCount] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

An audit log record says who changed what and when: the user, the action, the object and the old and new values. The Get-ZbxAuditLog cmdlet reads them with auditlog.get: all of them up to -Limit, by id with -Id or from the pipeline, or with the whole auditlog.get selection in -Filter. -User narrows the result to the audit log records of the given users, each a name, an id or a piped object. It writes ZabbixAuditLogRecord objects or, with -CountOutput, the number of matches; it needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Show the latest changes

```powershell
Get-ZbxAuditLog -SortField clock -SortOrder Descending -Limit 5 |
    Select-Object Time, Username, Action, ResourceName
```

Audit records are returned oldest first unless sorted; -SortField clock -SortOrder Descending with -Limit gives the newest. Action is a number (0 add, 1 update, 2 delete, 8 login ...).

### Example 2: Show what changed on one object

```powershell
$hour = [DateTimeOffset]::UtcNow.AddHours(-1).ToUnixTimeSeconds()
Get-ZbxAuditLog -Filter @{ filter = @{ resourcename = 'web-02' }; time_from = $hour } |
    Select-Object Action, Details
```

-Filter takes auditlog.get's own parameters: here the records whose resourcename is the host, in the last hour. Details holds the changed fields as JSON.

### Example 3: List a user's logins

```powershell
Get-ZbxAuditLog -User 'Admin' -Filter @{ filter = @{ action = 8 }; limit = 5 } -SortField clock -SortOrder Descending |
    Select-Object Time, Ip
```

-User takes a username, id or object; with -Filter the server keeps only action 8 (login), newest first.
